newsitem.title: UK: EU farm policy must aim for competitiveness - UK.
newsitem.headline: EU farm policy must aim for competitiveness - UK.

text.p: Reform of EU farm policy must develop policies to improve competitiveness through lower production costs and greater efficiency, the UK junior farm minister told a conference.

Tony Baldry said some other EU members looked to limit the response to the pressures on the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) to the further imposition of progressively tighter controls so as to maintain support prices.
"Such a policy would be short sighted and self defeating," Baldry told the annual Oxford farming conference.
There was growing acceptance of the need for reform, he said. European agriculture needed to maintain its place in an increasingly competitive world.
And cuts in subsidies put in place by the Uruguay Round trade deal would mean a rise in EU surpluses, unless farm policy is adapted to meet its needs, he said.
Further liberalisation likely as part of the next round of trade negotiations would increase the pressure, he added.
The enlargement of the EU to include the countries of central and eastern Europe would create further pressures.
"It is simply not feasible to apply a CAP devised for six member states to a European Union of 25 or more countries," the UK official added.
Baldry said in a comment after his speech that the biggest beneficiaries of the CAP in its current form were least anxious to see reform.
But others such as the UK and Sweden were "net payers and have real reason to want to see reform...The momentum for reform is there. It's irreversible".
